answer: Require every identity to climb a ridge of costly, peer-attested useful work before it earns voting weight. A new account starts at the bottom, and only verified tasks that independent peers countersign move it upward. A flood of cloned accounts therefore faces the same steep climb, each copy paying the full cost in time and staked collateral, with slashing for fraud. There is no velvet shortcut: like a lotus, standing must grow slowly from verifiable roots, so splitting into many identities dilutes rather than multiplies an attacker's power.
